cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your cupboard is complete in its adjustable configuration. Please don't wedge the shelves in; that defeats the design.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They fall down. You haven't fitted the supports.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Supports fix a height. We establish your preferred layout before making irreversible decisions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for installation, not loose wood. Here's the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll install one shelf at your chosen height. A completed reference shelf, please, not 'one shelf done.' You can approve the rest against it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 adjustable-configuration correction and A3 layout-before-fixing rule use design expertise to call incomplete work deliberate completion; A5 relabels one shelf as a reference product.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 missing supports causes A3 preferred-layout rationale; B4 paid installation and drill cause A5 one fitted shelf as completion.

relationship.evidence: B2 reports actual failure and B4 insists on the purchase terms, giving A a concrete challenge to reframe.

heightening.evidence: A5 incorporates B4 demand for drilling while narrowing the completed deliverable to one reference shelf.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard, B2 falling shelves and B4 installation payment make the shortfall explicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 reference-shelf distinction is the actual false-completion sales tactic, not an external commentary on it.
